title: PromptOasis journey lab notes
body:
Quick contextual brain-dump for a small product spike: 'PromptOasis' = lightweight guided prompt onramp + journey scaffolding for new users and power users who want reusable, composable prompt seeds. Rough PRD-ish notes, user stories, tech constraints, and a rollout thought-path.

Purpose / hypothesis:
- Hypothesis: many teams building on Redwood adopt ad-hoc prompt templates; onboarding + discoverability gap leads to slower time-to-first-production and higher token waste.
- Purpose: create a tiny surface in the Console + API that lets users craft, test, and pin 'journey seeds' (mini prompt cartridges) that can be: saved, versioned, and surfaced to teammates.

Goals (MVP):
- Seed editor (single text + metadata) with quick test playground (1-2 prompts)
- Tagging & discoverability inside Console (public/private stacks)
- API to reference a seed by id in downstream requests (lightweight: seed_id param that attaches prompt prefix)
- Basic analytics: usage counter, avg token delta relative to blank baseline

Success metrics (initial):
- 30% reduction in token waste for teams that adopt seeds (measured by before/after anchor set)
- 15% faster time-to-first-successful-gen (tracked via onboarding funnel)
- 3 beta teams actively author seeds in first 6 weeks

Primary user flows (sketch):
1) New user guided flow: "Start with a seed" -> shows 3 curated seeds by category (assistant, summarizer, code-exec) -> user picks, opens editor, runs quick test -> saves to team library.
2) Developer flow: add seed_id to API call or route config; platform applies prefix (with optional ephemeral params) before model.
3) Team admin: pin/unpin seeds, mark canonical, view usage.

Core UX components:
- Seed editor: name, one-sentence intent, prompt body (multi-line), placeholders for {{user_input}}, optional safety hints
- Quick test panel: small chat-like runner with history = 3 messages
- Library view: filter by tags, sort by recent/usage/owner
- Placement: Console -> 'Prompt Lab' under Hosted API -> quick connector to SDK examples

Edge cases / constraints:
- Avoid storing PII inside saved seeds (TODO: redact / warn)
- Seed prefix length might push inputs over model max tokens; need validation + soft warning
- Versioning: lightweight increment (v1, v2) + rollback to previous
- Permission model: team-level shared seeds vs private drafts

Engineering notes (rough):
- Minimal backend: seeds table (id, owner_id, org_id, name, body, tags, visibility, version, created_at) -> small CRUD service behind Console. Keep size small to avoid big infra changes.
- API change: allow optional seed_id on generation endpoints. Server-side expands seed into prefix; token accounting should attribute seed tokens to "seed overhead" for cost insights.
- Cache: consider caching compiled seed templates for hot ones to avoid expensive parsing at inference time.
- Fallback policy: if seed references unavailable model-specific tokens (e.g., model-specific system prompts), strip with warning.

Security / compliance / privacy notes:
- Default to private seeds. Public visibility must be explicit.
- Audit log events for create/edit/delete (for Private/Enterprise customers) -> linkable to KMS/HSM compliance checklist.

Potential experiments / variants:
- 'Economy seeds' that use compact placeholders and suggest quantization-friendly phrasing for token saving
- Seed templates with recommended batching knobs (e.g., batch friendly where seeds use fewer tokens but more deterministic instructions)
- Auto-suggest: derive seed candidates from high-quality user prompts seen in org usage (privacy-safeguarded)

Open questions / risks:
- Ownership model for community-curated seeds (IP, licensing)
- How to show the token cost impact without scaring non-technical users? (UI: show "seed adds ~X tokens (est.)" with link to cost explainer)
- SDK ergonomics: should we expand SDK to have seed management or keep seeds Console-only + seed_id pass-through?

Rolling plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
- Week 0-2: prototype editor in Console + CRUD API; wire-up a fake local seed driver for manual testing
- Week 3-5: implement seed expansion in hosted generation path, basic analytics, internal dogfood with two teams
- Week 6-8: invite 3 external beta customers, add permissions and audit logs, refine UX
- Post-GA: integrate with rollouts (pin seed to a rollout bucket), surface seed-driven regressions in Optimize (link seed -> evals)

Quick mock API snippet (informal):
- POST /v1/generate { model, input, seed_id: "s_9d3f", options: {temperature:0.2}}
- server: lookup seed -> prefix = seed.body.replace("{{user_input}}", input) -> run generation

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Create initial Jira (ENG-4921) for backend + API; link to confluence page and assign eng owner.
- Sketch Console wireframe and drop into #prod-console channel for feedback (Mira to lead).
- Quick legal check on ownership + sharing (Keisha).
- Small privacy experiment: run auto-suggest algorithm on anonymized org logs (requires SRE input).

Loose user stories (for backlog):
- As a product manager, I want to save a repeatable prompt pattern so teammates can reuse it reliably.
- As a developer, I want to pass seed_id in my requests so I can centralize prompt edits without changing client code.
- As a team admin, I want to pin a canonical seed so the org uses a vetted instruction set.

Last random thoughts (freeform):
- Could be a nice surface to ship with "starter packs" for common verticals (support agent, summarizer, code helper) -> low lift marketing collateral.
- Keep scope intentionally small for v1: saved text + tags, no heavy templating or runtime paramization. If adoption is high, expand to templates with typed placeholders and example datasets.

End of dump. Will refine into a cleaner PRD if team wants to push forward.
